harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired node1’s reservation utility with atomic, idempotent SQLite transactions and bounded lock waits. Existing stock and reservations remain intact, and the repair persisted across reboot.
actions_performed: Serialized reservation processing with BEGIN IMMEDIATE and a five-second busy timeout.
Made stock decrement conditional and atomic, preventing negative inventory.
Implemented idempotent replay of successful request IDs.
Verified concurrent requests, rejection behavior, lock timeout, and database integrity.
Restarted node1 and verified changed boot identity, recovered system health, persisted code, and preserved data.
Kept RHEL 7.9, kernel 3.10.0-1160, Python 2.7, and SQLite 3.7 unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Atomic exactly-once reservations with nonnegative stock under competition
evidence.summary: Two simultaneous 4-unit requests against stock=5 produced one success and one insufficient-stock rejection; remaining stock was 1 and integrity_check was ok.

evidence.requirement: Successful request ID replay returns its earlier result without another decrement
evidence.summary: Retry output matched the original result, only one reservation row existed, and stock remained unchanged; live previous-request replay also returned stored quantity 2 with stock still 5.

evidence.requirement: Positive quantity validation and insufficient-stock rejection
evidence.summary: Zero and negative quantities returned validation errors without changing reservations; the competing request exceeding remaining stock was rejected.
A deliberately held write lock caused a controlled rc=4 failure after five seconds, with no reservation or stock mutation.

evidence.requirement: Repair installed compatibly while preserving existing data
evidence.summary: The installed Python 2-compatible implementation compiled successfully; database integrity remained ok and previous-request quantity=2 was preserved.

Healthy baseline boot ID 809708f3-1c5f-4e37-ad6a-8bcbae408799 was captured; reboot was acknowledged; post-restart boot ID changed to df1448c7-7d5a-481e-8a84-e70d46fd5646; system returned running, the repair checksum persisted, integrity_check was ok, and stock/reservation data remained intact.
